en: The Sūtra of the Fundamental Secret Divine Mantra of Amitābha Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci by Imperial Decree during the Cao Wei Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying in the Kingdom of Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly...
The assembly of the Bhagavat consisted of one thousand two hundred and fifty people,
all of whom were great Arhats renowned to the world: the Elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Cūḍapanthaka, Nanda, Ānanda, Rāhula, and Kapphiṇa.
Panthaka, Piṇḍola-bharadvāja, Kālodāyin, Mahākapphiṇa, Vakkula, Aniruddha,
and other such great disciples, together with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas Mañjuśrī the Dharma Prince, Ajita Bodhisattva, Gandhahasti Bodhisattva, and Nityodyukta.
The Bodhisattva was together with such great bodhisattvas as these, as well as a vast assembly of devas, including Śakra Devānām Indra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Elder Śāriputra: "From here, to the west, passing through a hundred thousand koṭis of buddha-fields, there is..."
The world is named Sukhāvatī; in that land there is a Buddha named Amitābha who currently dwells and expounds the Dharma.
Śāriputra, for what reason is that land called Sukhāvatī? Because the sentient beings in that country have no manifold sufferings and experience only various joys, it is therefore named Sukhāvatī.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the land of Ultimate Bliss is surrounded on all sides by sevenfold railings, sevenfold decorative nets, and sevenfold rows of trees, all composed of the four precious substances; for this reason, that land is named Ultimate Bliss.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the Land of Ultimate Bliss there are ponds made of the seven treasures, filled with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.
Their bottoms are entirely covered with golden sand, and their four sides and stairways are composed of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and white jade.
Above them are multi-storied pavilions, likewise adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musaragalva, red pearl, and agate.
Adorned with lotuses in its ponds as large as chariot wheels— blue with blue radiance, yellow with yellow radiance, red with red radiance,
and white with white radiance— subtle, fragrant, and pure; Śāriputra, the Land of Ultimate Bliss is thus adorned with such meritorious qualities.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-land celestial music constantly plays and the ground is made of gold; six times throughout the day and night, *māndārava* flowers rain down.

The sentient beings of that land always at dawn each take a fold of their robes to gather various wonderful flowers as offerings to ten trillion buddhas in other directions, and then, at the time for a meal, they return to their own land to eat.
Śāriputra, the land of Sukhāvatī is adorned with such meritorious qualities as these.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, that land is always filled with various wonderful birds of diverse colors—white cranes, peacocks, parrots, śārikas, kalaviṅkas, and *saṃjīvaka* birds.
These flocks of birds, throughout the six periods of day and night, [chant the praises of the Buddha].

At that time, they emit harmonious and elegant sounds; these sounds expound and clarify such dharmas as the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
When the sentient beings of that land hear these sounds, they all recollect the Buddha, recollect the Dharma, and recollect the Sangha.
Śāriputra, do not think that these birds are actually born as a result of karmic retribution for transgressions. Why is this? Because those...
Śāriputra, in that buddha-field there are no three evil destinies; even the names of the three evil paths do not exist, let alone their actual presence.
All these birds are transformations produced by Amitābha Buddha, intended to cause the sound of the Dharma to circulate.
Śāriputra, when the gentle breeze blows through the rows of jewel-trees in that buddha-field, it...
Furthermore, from the precious lattices, subtle and wondrous sounds emerge, like a hundred thousand kinds of music performed simultaneously;
those who hear these sounds naturally give rise to thoughts of mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Sangha.
Śāriputra, that buddha-land is thus adorned with the accomplishment of such meritorious virtues.
"What do you think, Śāriputra? For what reason is that Buddha named Amitābha? Śāriputra, the light of that Buddha is immeasurable;
it illumines the lands of the ten directions without obstruction. For this reason, he is named Amitābha.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the lifespan of that Buddha, as well as that of his people, is immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas."
Therefore, he is named Amitābha. Śāriputra, since that Buddha Amitābha attained Buddhahood, ten kalpas have passed until now.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, that Buddha has immeasurable and boundless śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats;
they cannot be known by means of calculation. The multitude of bodhisattvas is likewise so. Śāriputra, that Buddha—
The land is adorned with such meritorious qualities as these.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, all those born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss are non-retrogressive (avaivartika);
among them, there are many who are in their last birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha), so numerous that they cannot be known by calculation, but can only...
Śāriputra, throughout immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, I have expounded this;
those sentient beings who hear it should make a vow to be born in that land. Why is this? Because one shall be able to dwell together in one place with such supreme and virtuous people.
Śāriputra, one cannot be born in that land by means of roots of goodness, merit, or causal conditions that are meager.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, Amitābha Buddha possesses a fundamental secret dhāraṇī mantra known as the "Mantra for Uprooting All Karmic Obstructions and Attaining Birth in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

He then spoke the mantra: [The mantra follows] Śāriputra, this is the fundamental secret dhāraṇī mantra of Amitābha Buddha, named the "Mantra for Uprooting All Karmic Obstructions and Attaining Birth in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. He then spoke the mantra: [The mantra follows]
Namo Amitābhāya Tathāgatāya (1) Tadyathā (2) Amṛte (3) Dhupavi (4) Amṛte (5) Siddhampavi (6) Amṛte (7) Vikaraṇate (8) Amṛte (9) Vikaraṇḍe (10)
(11) *Gāminī* (12) *Gagana* (13) *Cittakāre* (14) *Svāhā*. (15) The Buddha said:

"If there are good sons or good daughters who are able to recite this mantra, Amitābha Buddha will constantly abide upon their crowns, protecting them day and night so that no enemies may find an opportunity against them; they shall always attain peace in the present life."
When the time of death arrives, one will naturally and spontaneously be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the name of Amitābha Buddha is endowed with immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, profoundly secret, supreme, subtle, and unsurpassed merit. Why is this so? Because of Amitābha Buddha...

Within these three characters are contained all the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Arhats, as well as all sūtras, dhāraṇīs, divine mantras, and immeasurable practices and dharmas.
Therefore, the name of that Buddha is itself the unsurpassed, true, and ultimate Dharma of the Mahāyāna; it is itself the unsurpassed excellence.
The supreme, pure, definitive, and wondrous practice is for the sake of the unsurpassed, most excellent, and subtle dhāraṇī;
thus he spoke these verses:
The letter A is the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time; The letter Mi is all the Bodhisattvas.
The eighty thousand sacred teachings are fully contained within these three characters.

Śāriputra, if there are sentient beings who, upon hearing the discourse on the inconceivable merit of Amitābha Buddha, rejoice with leaping joy, wholeheartedly recite his name, and believe deeply without slackening, they shall experience incomparable bliss in their present bodies; or—
One may transform poverty and low status to attain wealth and nobility; or, by attaining the fruits [of practice], escape the suffering of illness pursued by past karma;

or, transform a short lifespan to obtain longevity; or, transform the resentment of enemies to achieve the flourishing of descendants and peace of body and mind, with all wishes fulfilled as desired. Such merits are beyond measure.
Śāriputra, if there are good men or good women who, upon hearing the teaching of Amitābha Buddha,
hold fast to his name— whether for one day, two days, three days, four days, five days, six days, or seven days— with single-mindedness and without distraction,
exclusively holding fast to the name, then by virtue of this recitation of the name, all their transgressions will be extinguished; this is...

Śāriputra, by virtue of many roots of goodness, merit, and favorable conditions, when such a person approaches the end of life, Amitābha Buddha, together with his assembly of holy ones, will appear before them.
At the moment of death, their mind will not be inverted, and they will immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha.
Śāriputra, because I see this benefit, I speak these words: "If there are sentient beings..."
Those who hear this teaching should make a vow to be born in that land.
Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable merit of Amitābha Buddha,
there are likewise in the eastern direction Akṣobhya Buddha, Merudhvaja Buddha, Mahameru Buddha, Meruprabhāsa Buddha, and Ruciraketu Buddha.
The Buddha Ghoṣa and other Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each from their respective lands, extend their broad and long tongues,
completely covering the trichiliocosm, and speak these words of truth: "You sentient beings,
you should believe this Sūtra on the Praise of Inconceivable Merit, which is protected and remembered by all Buddhas."

Śāriputra, in the worlds of the southern direction there are Buddhas such as Candrasūryapradīpa, Yaśaḥprabha, Mahājvālāṃsa, Merupradīpa, and Anantavīrya—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Each of these Buddhas, in their respective lands, extends his broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm, and utters words of truth: "You..."
All sentient beings should believe in this *Sūtra on the Immeasurable Praise of Meritorious Virtues and the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas*.
Śāriputra, in the western world-system there are the Buddha Amitāyus, the Buddha Amitābha, and the Buddha Amitadhvaja.
The Buddha Great Light, the Buddha Great Radiance, the Buddha Jewel Mark, the Buddha Pure Light, and other Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each within their respective lands,
extended their broad and long tongues until they completely covered the trichiliocosm and spoke words of truth:
"You sentient beings, you should believe these words of praise concerning the inconceivable merit extolled by all Buddhas."
"Śāriputra, in the worlds of the northern direction, there are Buddhas such as Arciṣkandha, Varaghoṣa, Duṣprasaha, Sūryagarbha, and Jālinīprabha—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Each of these Buddhas, in their respective lands, extends his broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm, and speaks words of truth to you, the assembly: [Listen!]"
"Śāriputra, you should believe this *Sūtra on the Inconceivable Merits of Rebirth*, which is praised by all Buddhas and protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas.
In the world-system below, there are Buddhas such as Siṃha Buddha, Yaśas Buddha, Nāma Buddha, Kīrti Buddha, Dharma Buddha,
Dharmadhvaja Buddha, and Dharmadhara Buddha— Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each appearing in their respective lands."
With his broad and long tongue, he completely covers the trichiliocosm while speaking words of truth:
"You sentient beings, you should believe this Sutra on the Praise of Inconceivable Merit, which is protected and remembered by all Buddhas."
Śāriputra, in the worlds above, there are Buddhas such as Brahma-voice Buddha, Constellation King Buddha, Supreme Fragrance Buddha, Fragrant Light Buddha, Great Flame Shoulder Buddha,
Adorned Body with Various Colored Jewel Flower Buddha, Śāla Tree King Buddha, Jewel Flower Virtue Buddha, Seeing All Meanings Buddha,
and Tathāgata Like Mount Sumeru Buddha; these and other Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each—
From within that land, he extended his broad and long tongue, covering the entire trichiliocosm, and spoke these truthful words: "You sentient beings,
you should believe this Sutra on the Praise of Inconceivable Merit, which is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas."
"Śāriputra, what do you think? For what reason is this called 'The Sūtra Protected and Kept in Mind by All Buddhas'?

Śāriputra, if there are sons or daughters of good family who hear these names spoken by all the Buddhas and the title of this sūtra, all such sons and daughters of good family shall be collectively protected and kept in mind by all the Buddhas."
All shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, Śāriputra, you and all others should believe and accept my words as well as what has been spoken by all the Buddhas.
Śāriputra, if there are those who have already made a vow, are now making a vow, or will make a vow, desiring to be born in the land of Amitābha Buddha—all such persons...
All shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;

whether they have already been born, are now being born, or will hereafter be born in that land. For this reason, Śāriputra, any good man or good woman who possesses faith should make a vow to be born in that land.

Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable merits of all those Buddhas, so too do those Buddhas proclaim my own inconceivable merits, saying: "The Buddha Śākyamuni is able to perform a most difficult and rare feat;
he is able, within the Sahā world-system, during this evil age of the five turbidities and the kalpa-turbidity..."
"Śāriputra, you should know that within the defilement of views, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of sentient beings, and the defilement of lifespan,
I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and preached to all sentient beings this Dharma which is difficult for all the world to believe;
I have performed this difficult task and attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this evil world of the five defilements."
"To preach this dharma so difficult to believe for the sake of all the world is truly most difficult. When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
Śāriputra, the bhikṣus, and all those in the world— gods, humans, asuras, and others— hearing what the Buddha had spoken,
rejoiced, accepted it with faith, paid their respects, and departed.
The Sutra on the Fundamental Secret Divine Mantra of Amitābha Buddha Spoken by the Buddha:
Resolving Doubts Regarding the Authenticity of the Divine Mantra Sutra.
It states that among the Tripiṭaka, there is the "Mantra for Eradicating All Karmic Obstructions and Attaining Rebirth in the Pure Land" (found in the *Xiaozhuan*).
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* was retranslated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Liu Song dynasty by imperial decree.

It comprises a total of fifty-nine characters and fifteen phrases. Furthermore, regarding the merit of reciting the mantra, there are twenty-seven characters—beginning with "If there is a good man" (乃至) and ending with "spontaneously attaining rebirth"—which are present in all extant texts of this scripture but were absent from the previous [version].
Regarding the subsequent passages—both those preceding and following them—they are entirely identical to the minor sutras translated by Kumārajīva without any difference.
The sections inserted in the middle concerning divine mantras and the exposition of merits were translated by Ratnamati;
therefore, he used the passage beginning with "The letter A pervades the ten directions" as the Buddha’s own words, intending to suppress other scriptures and exalt this one.

Is this not a spurious fabrication produced by those of later generations who follow heterodox pride? There are no small number of doubts and difficulties; yet, when examining various catalogs, this scripture is not recorded therein.
(First) The preceding and following passages of this scripture, though containing some redundant wording, are not slightly different from the minor scriptures translated by Kumārajīva.
Since the translators are different, how could the phrasing be identical? (Second) Based on the inconceivable [power] of Amitābha...

*The Transmission of Supernatural Power* (the *Shenli zhuan* is found in the Tibetan edition). Did Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna, wishing to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nourishment (*An-yang*), receive this dhāraṇī through a dream?
The Tripiṭaka Master Naśa recited this dhāraṇī; Dharma Master Xiū of T'ien-p'ing Temple received it orally from the Tripiṭaka Master Naśa.
That man said, "The manuscript of this sūtra does not come from foreign lands. (Text: Received the record [it contains the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* bestowed upon him]).
(3) The record states that during Nāgārjuna’s translation assembly at Yeshé (Yaśas), the original manuscript was not obtained; how much more so since it did not come from abroad?

If the manuscript of the sutra had not yet been transmitted, who could have translated it? (4) Furthermore, in the *Biographies of Kumārajīva* (Tang Biographies 1, *Shijiao Lu* 6, etc.), no mention is found of this sutra being translated.
(5) Such is the general outline of this spurious sutra; how can it be considered an authentic scripture? [Response:]
It is said that because it was not included in the catalogs and did not circulate— just as, for example,

the *Śīlamahāyāna-śāstra* (Shè mómóhēnyán lùn) did not circulate in the land of Han for seven hundred years (the fact that the commentary did not circulate in the land of Han appears in one fascicle of the *Tōngfǎ shù*)—

it is one of the difficult points regarding discrepancies among different translations, yet its wording is entirely identical; for example, the *Amitābha-sūtra* translated by Kumārajīva and [this version].

The text of the *Smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* translated by Guṇabhadra is identical and not different [from other versions], as seen in the twelfth fascicle, the fourteenth fascicle, and the seventeenth fascicle of the *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu*.

Furthermore, regarding the *Awakening of Faith* translated by Paramārtha and Mādhyamika (Mādhyamika being the translator of the commentary; the original text of the commentary is the *Awakening...*)... [text truncated]
This is a treatise on faith. The wording is no different from that of [the *Avataṃsaka*] which unifies the three [vehicles].

As for those who did not accept it, Nāgārjuna compiled its Sanskrit original, which consisted of one hundred thousand [verses]. According to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Upper Version contained as many verses as there are atoms in ten trichiliocosms and as many chapters as there are atoms in a four-continent world system;

the Middle Version contained four hundred and ninety-eight thousand eight hundred verses and one thousand two hundred chapters; the Lower Version contained one hundred thousand verses and forty-eight chapters; and the Abridged Version is the current eighty-fascicle edition of this very division. [Thus it was] brought forth.

In the three-fascicle *Commentary on the "Chapter on Vows"* (*Yuàn pǐn shū cāo*), it is stated: "How much more so within the 'Difficulties and Reprimands' (*Nán hē zhōng*) it says clearly that [the foreigner] did not come, but was in the land of India" (Meeting 3).

Furthermore, in the "Foreigner Did Not Come" section, because the words could not be obtained, they are attributed to the period before he had crossed [to China] (Meeting 4). As for why [the name] is not mentioned in the biography of Paramārtha (*Liúzhī chuán*):

among the sutras and śāstras translated by him, those most widely circulated are already fully recorded; why then would the biography of Paramārtha mention [him]? (The biography of Paramārtha states: "Paramārtha...")
Within this room, there are ten thousand fascicles of Sanskrit manuscripts of the sūtras and śāstras; the newly revised texts have filled an entire room with draft copies taken down by a scribe.
(Text) With ten thousand fascicles filling the interior of the room, does one truly possess a "finger-in-the-palm" mastery of these scriptures?
May those who study them not dare to give rise to slander; may they instead take the merit of this single proofreading to bring peace and happiness to themselves and others in future lives.
Written by Chikuyo Chishaku, the ninth incumbent of Ryūgen-ji in Kamigōrin,
Bushū, during the latter half of the ninth month in the eleventh year of the Genroku era.
